baer-heitev/1:ב: (ב) peace — that they regret sitting in darkness. Bach wrote if he has no bread he need not kindle first — so Eliyah Rabbah; but Taz wrote bread first — end. Magen Avraham wrote: perhaps nowadays since we kindle inside he should acquire a Hanukkah light, yet he should not sit in darkness; even though forbidden to eat by its light, since impossible otherwise it is like danger — place it on his table even though he will use it — so too on weekdays one who has only one candle — end.
levushei-serad/1:_: {Rama: Magen Avraham s.k. 2} And possible — this contradicts his words in siman 673 s.k. 2 where he proved from here that even to eat with him is forbidden — end; however here he speaks possibly; above he wrote what seemed to him primary.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) Because of peace of his household — some say nowadays since kindling inside one should acquire a Hanukkah light since he will not sit in darkness; even though forbidden to use its light, it is like danger as above siman 671 seif 5 — place on table; but most Acharonim agree not to distinguish between Gemara times and ours.
turei-zahav/1:ב: He should acquire a Hanukkah light. Ran and Beit Yosef wrote: although Kiddush is d'oraisa and Hanukkah light is d'rabbanan, since one can sanctify on bread with Hanukkah oil it is preferable — end; per this if he has no bread, bread is preferable since he must sanctify on it d'oraisa. Rambam wrote here Hanukkah light and Kiddush of the day are both d'rabbanan and Hanukkah light precedes Kiddush of the day because of publicizing the miracle — if so even without bread Hanukkah light is preferable. However it appears for bread all agree bread comes first: what is written siman 271 that Kiddush precedes meal needs — that means other meal needs such as dishes; they called it in Gemara Berachot chapter 10 "honor of the day." But bread — lechem mishneh — precedes wine of Kiddush, for lechem mishneh is d'oraisa for all as R' Abba said in chapter 27 "lechem mishneh"; three meals too are d'oraisa and we require bread as siman 274 — all the more so it precedes Hanukkah light which is only d'rabbanan.
